open_questions: Why is one transit strongly negative (-3592 ppm, -5.7 sigma) and transit depths inconsistent (p_consistent 3.988608947524869e-09)? Likely spot crossing on Teff 3439 K M dwarf but needs ground-based transit photometry to confirm depth ~6400 ppm at 12.7 d.

Does QLP non-detection (sector 91 depth 1743 +/- 1066 ppm) reflect true dilution/systematics versus systematics? Joint TESS-SPOC follow-up and centroid difference imaging in upcoming sectors will test on-target origin.
dossier.public_summary: A 3.4 Earth-radius, 12.7-day dip repeats in TESS data on a nearby M dwarf with a flat bottom and no sign of a stellar binary, and no nearby star within one TESS pixel can plausibly mimic it. The dip appears shallow in one low-quality pipeline and one transit looks inverted, which points to spot systematics on the variable star rather than a blended eclipse, so a planet remains the best explanation pending ground-based follow-up to confirm the depth.

reasons.why: Apparent depth change is a calibration difference between QLP and TESS-SPOC (high S/N detection in two TESS-SPOC sectors, non-detection in QLP at large error). Alone sectors.p_constant is never a reject.
reasons.value: p_constant 9.849e-7; sector_depths_by_source verdict differs_by_source: QLP 1743 ppm ( err 1066) vs TESS-SPOC 8347 ppm ( err 668, p_constant 0.771)

reasons.why: Inconsistent individual transit depths, including a deep negative outlier, argues for spot/crowding systematics on a faint M dwarf but does not by itself show an EB; signal remains repeatable at period 12.7 d in vetted light curve.
